discussion_comments.comment_body: This fetches every remote head SHA before the user has confirmed anything. On repos with many branches that can download a lot of history just to list unpublished commits. Consider limiting it to the upstream/default branch or using local remote-tracking refs.

Partially addressed in #15371: if an advertised remote head equals local HEAD, preparation skips the history fetch because that proves the ancestry is already published. Otherwise it still fetches advertised heads without updating remote-tracking refs or FETCH_HEAD. Limiting that fallback to one branch or stale local refs can misclassify published history and incorrectly reject sensitive paths. Further fetch optimization is deferred; this does not eliminate the large-repository cost in the fallback case.

Valid, fixed. The body is now read incrementally and the reader is cancelled as soon as the running total passes the limit, so a missing or wrong `Content-Length` can't make it buffer the whole response. The limit is also a `maxArchiveBytes` option (default 100 MB). Covered by "stops reading an archive once it exceeds the size limit", which uses an endless stream with no Content-Length and asserts it stops after a few chunks.

Fixed in b7fd827e5b. Command timeouts now use a coalesced, bounded client.list health probe. A successful probe or any other command reply arriving during it keeps the socket and SSH forward alive; only a failed probe with no intervening replies retires the transport. Regression tests cover a slow read with an unrelated pending write, a slow heartbeat while writes receive replies, concurrent timeout probe coalescing, and the real one-way forwarding stall. Writes and prompts are never replayed.

This is now awaited on every session build, so model discovery lands on the task-start path for the first time.

Agent review: 

Only the primary call is bounded, though: when `/api/v1/models` fails, the
fallback `fetchModelIdsFromSource` uses a bare `fetch` with no timeout, so
against a host that drops packets rather than refusing (remote LM Studio, VPN
down) the 5s abort fires and then the fallback hangs — and the task never
starts. Localhost is fine; a closed port fails immediately.

The unbounded fetch is pre-existing, but it previously only stalled webview
surfaces. An AbortSignal in `fetchModelIdsFromSource` would cover it.
